name: Statora Plus
author: Panagiotis Pavlidis

sections.description:
All your key product stats. One clear view.

Understand your WooCommerce store at a glance. Statora Plus brings essential product-performance statistics together in one clear dashboard, helping you monitor and compare products without searching through scattered reports.

Built around three principles: Reliability, Simplicity and Autonomy.

Statora Plus combines WooCommerce order data with its own product-page view tracking system to provide a clearer picture of product performance.

The plugin’s administration interface is currently available in Greek only.

Requires WooCommerce to be installed and activated.

Features

  • Store overview with product views, orders, units sold, revenue, cancellations and returns.
  • Product-level statistics in one table.
  • Today and overall figures for supported metrics.
  • Search products by name or SKU.
  • Sort product results using supported metrics or sortable table columns.
  • View product stock where stock management is enabled.
  • Uses WooCommerce order data and records product-page views.

Important notes

  • Historical cancellation and refund event dates cannot be reconstructed when the original event history was not recorded. Today’s cancellation and return figures are available from the relevant tracking version onward; older events may not be represented.
  • Revenue and sold-unit metrics are recognized only after the merchant marks an order Completed, confirming customer receipt. Daily figures use the completion date. Cash on Delivery orders remain in Processing until payment is collected; mark them Completed only after delivery/payment confirmation.
  • Store overview counts one cancellation per order and one return per WooCommerce refund record. Product statistics attribute each event to the affected products.
  • A cancelled unpaid Cash on Delivery order counts only as a cancellation. A paid cancellation counts as a return only when a WooCommerce refund record exists. A full refund of a paid order, recorded before the order is marked Completed, counts as both a return and a cancellation, even when refunded quantities are not recorded. A full return after completion requires a full monetary refund and refunded quantities for every product line. A partial return counts as a return, not a cancellation.
  • For accurate product-level attribution and full-return detection, enter refunded quantities for the affected line items in the WooCommerce refund form. Amount-only partial refunds on multi-product orders cannot be assigned to a specific product. Manual WooCommerce refunds only record the refund in the store; return the money to the customer before creating the manual refund record.
  • WooCommerce manages stock reduction and temporary reservations. Statora Plus does not reduce stock itself, avoiding duplicate stock deductions. For unpaid Pending payment orders, configure WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Inventory > Hold stock (minutes).
  • Statistics are intended for product-performance monitoring and analysis, not as an accounting report.
  • Product-page views are recorded and counted by Statora Plus using its own tracking tables.
  • Review the dashboard after installation and allow the initial background import of existing WooCommerce order history to complete before evaluating historical order statistics.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the statora-plus folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory or install the ZIP through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate WooCommerce.
  3. Install and activate Statora Plus.
  4. Open Statora Plus from the WordPress admin menu and allow the initial background import of existing WooCommerce order history to complete.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin replace WooCommerce reports?

No. Statora Plus consolidates key product statistics in one view to make them easier to review and compare.

Are cancellation and return counts always available for all historical dates?

No. Historical event timestamps cannot be recreated if they were not recorded when the events occurred.

Does Statora Plus use its own product-view tracking system?

Yes. Statora Plus uses its own tracking system and database tables to record product-page views. No external analytics service is required for this built-in tracking.

How are cancellations and returns recorded?

Statora Plus uses WooCommerce order and refund records. Store overview figures count cancellation events per order and return events per WooCommerce refund record. Product-level statistics attribute events to the affected products when the necessary information is available.

Does a return count always mean that the physical product was received back?

No. Return statistics are based on WooCommerce refund records and the refunded quantities recorded in the order. Statora Plus does not independently verify the physical receipt of returned products.

Is the administration interface available in English?

Not yet. The plugin’s administration interface is currently available in Greek only.
sections.changelog:
0.11.46

  • Place narrowly scoped Plugin Check security-rule annotations on the database-call lines that use constructor-generated table identifiers.
  • Keep all SQL values prepared and preserve the existing query behavior.

0.11.45

  • Clarify narrowly scoped PHPCS suppressions for internally generated table identifiers and dynamically prepared integer ID lists.
  • Keep all SQL values prepared while retaining compatibility with the declared WordPress minimum version.

0.11.44

  • Preserve the earliest recorded cancellation timestamp when reconciling order-level and product-level events.
  • Prevent later order snapshot synchronization from shifting historical cancellations into the current day.

0.11.43

  • Clarify the dashboard explanations for full refunds before and after order completion.
  • Explain the recorded-payment requirement for full refunds before completion.
  • Explain that full returns after completion require all line-item quantities to be recorded as refunded.

0.11.42

  • Recognize a full monetary refund for a paid order before it is marked Completed as both a return and a cancellation, even if refunded quantities were not entered.
  • Keep full returns after completion dependent on a full monetary refund and all line-item quantities refunded.
  • Keep partial refunds as returns without creating a cancellation event.
  • Continue leaving stock management exclusively to WooCommerce.

0.11.41

  • Recognize revenue and sold units only when an order is marked Completed.
  • Track the completion timestamp for accurate daily revenue and unit metrics.
  • Separate order-level dashboard cancellation/return counts from product-level event attribution.
  • Count a full return as a cancellation only when the full order amount and all product quantities are refunded.
  • Track individual WooCommerce refund records by refund ID and avoid double-counting multi-product refunds in the store overview.
  • Leave stock management to WooCommerce while recognizing revenue and sold units only on completion.
  • Rebuild existing order snapshots once after upgrading so the new completion and refund rules are applied.

0.11.40

  • Make product-view tracking and reporting fully self-contained.
  • Remove obsolete compatibility code and standardize plugin SQL aliases.

0.11.38

  • Improve partial SKU search query handling and cache SKU lookup results.
  • Address Plugin Check performance and database query findings.

0.11.37

  • Address WordPress.org review feedback and preserve data during storage migration.

0.11.36

  • Release version update.

0.11.35

  • Restored the established SKU search implementation following review of the alternative query approach.

0.11.34

  • Current development version of the product statistics dashboard.
